title: policy.json: dispatch
description: Sizing ready items into tiers, the brief, and the dispatch plan (design parts 5.1 and 5.2). The tiers themselves (executor, model class, effort) are in the tiers section.

inline_globs.description: Paths the orchestrator edits itself (tier 0): an item whose touches all fall here, such as a tracker edit, is not dispatched.

sensitive_globs.description: Paths whose change raises an item one tier for blast radius: the build and release pipeline, dependency manifests, security-sensitive code, the project's own policy.

owner_review_areas.description: Areas whose output the owner reviews in person, such as UI: the brief asks the executor for a review pack. The tier still comes from sizing.

tier1_max_touches.description: The most touches globs an item may list and still be tier 1 (mechanical, fully specified work).

familiar_min_yield.description: Down one tier for familiar ground: the share of first-pass successes the lower tier must have had on this area and item kind.

familiar_min_samples.description: How many past dispatches at the lower tier, in the same area and kind, before familiar ground counts.

default_estimates.description: The token estimate per tier until there are enough similar past items. Replaced by the median of similar past items once there are estimate_min_samples of them and the median is within estimate_max_multiple of the default (one wrong figure cannot set the estimate).

estimate_min_samples.description: How many similar past completions (same area, kind and tier, with a token count) the estimate needs before their median replaces the tier's default. Below it the plan uses the default and says the sample is too small.

estimate_max_multiple.description: A median of similar past completions more than this many times the tier's default is not used: the plan uses the default and says why. An estimate set on the item itself is kept, with a note.

report_at_budget_multiple.description: The brief asks the executor to report at this multiple of its token budget, even if unfinished.

serialize_overlap_share.description: Hold an item back while running items already cover at least this share of its touches globs. Below it, overlapping items run in parallel and the later one rebases.

tier3_mode.description: How a tier-3 item runs by default: headless (a background claude -p run in its own worktree; its exit is the completion notice) or interactive (a session the owner starts and steers).

headless_permission_mode.description: The permission mode a headless tier-3 run starts in. The project's own allow and deny rules still apply.

stall_after.description: Seconds a dispatch may show no progress before the watchdog (hitld dispatch watch) calls it stalled. Progress is what the executor does not have to send: commits and file changes in its worktree, tool calls and tokens from the harness, a headless run's output. This is the time for a tier-1 dispatch at its tier's default estimate; it is scaled by stall_tier_scale and by the dispatch's estimate.

deadline.description: Seconds from a dispatch's start to its finish, for a tier-1 dispatch at its tier's default estimate, scaled as stall_after is. A dispatch past it climbs the watchdog's ladder even while it shows progress.

stall_tier_scale.description: How much longer stall_after and deadline are per tier.

stall_estimate_max.description: stall_after and deadline grow with the dispatch's token estimate over its tier's default estimate, up to this many times. A smaller estimate never shortens them.

poke_wait.description: Seconds the watchdog waits after poking a stalled dispatch before it takes the next step of the ladder, if nothing has progressed since.

redispatch_max.description: How many times the watchdog abandons a stalled item and dispatches it afresh before the next failure becomes a question for the owner instead.

brief_kb.description: Knowledge-base pages a brief points to, per area: page paths with an optional #section.
